描述_ZN: Scroll of "Hibiscus and Golden Rooster", painted by Zhao Ji, Emperor Huizong of the Northern Song Dynasty, on silk, with color. 81.5 cm in length and 53.6 cm in width.　　As a separate painting discipline, Song dynasty flower and bird paintings had reached a high level of artistry in terms of both painting technique and expression, and "Hibiscus and Brocade Rooster" is one of the finest. This painting is a flower and bird painting depicting a golden autumn scene. In the picture, the hibiscus is in full bloom, gently trembling in the wind, and the butterflies are chasing and playing with each other, attracting the pheasants that fall on the branches to gaze back and stare. On the upper right side of this painting, Zhao Ji of Emperor Huizong of Song Dynasty inscribed in a lean gold font, "Autumn is strong and resists frost. It has been known to have all five virtues, and is more at ease than the eider duck", with the inscription "Xuanhedian imperial system and calligraphy" on the lower right and "One person in the world" in cursive script. Chicken in China has always been "virtuous bird", "Han Shi Wai Zhuan" contains: "the chicken has five virtues: head wearing a crown, also; foot fighting distance, also; enemy in front, dare to fight, also brave; see the food to call, also benevolent; guard the night not lost, also letter", can be seen in both civil and military, benevolent and brave, faithful and dedicated, It is no wonder that the emperor of the generation with the greatest talent also left the poem "Known to be full of five virtues, ease is better than eider ducks", revealing the praise for the noble character of ease, thus reflecting the humanistic meaning of Chinese flower and bird painting.　　In the works of Zhao Ji, the artistic style is very different from that of the simple and elegant ones, such as "Hibiscus and Pheasant" and "Mountain Bird with Plum Blossoms" (in the collection of the National Palace Museum, Taipei), and the simple and awkward ones such as "Willow Crow" (in the collection of the Shanghai Museum) and "Bird with Loquat and Mountain". Through a comparative analysis of brush and ink styles, Mr. Xu Bangda points out that the former is not by Zhao Ji, but by the painter of the Academy, while the latter is his own handwriting, a view shared by most art historical researchers. In addition, the extant record of the Southern Song court's collection of paintings in volume 3 of the "Southern Song Pavilion Continued Records" includes this painting in the category of "imperial inscriptions" alongside "imperial paintings," suggesting that the "Hibiscus and Golden Rooster" is merely a poem inscribed by Zhao Ji himself.
